title: Journey of Sound to the Brain
creator: NIDCD (NIH). No producer or animation studio named on the NIDCD page, the NIH STEM page (science.education.nih.gov/resource-materials/141) or the YouTube description (NIH channel, video eQEaiZ2j9oc, uploaded 2018-11-21).
license_quote: "Information on our website is in the public domain." NIDCD policies (https://www.nidcd.nih.gov/policies): "Unless otherwise stated, the information on this site is not copyrighted and is in the public domain." and "You may encounter documents that were sponsored along with private companies or other organizations. Those documents will have statements that protect them under U.S. and foreign copyright laws."
why: No copyright notice found and NIDCD's default is public domain, but the producer is never named, so contractor rights cannot be ruled out. The only copy offered is a YouTube embed; downloading from YouTube would be a rip, which our rules forbid. Usable only if an official downloadable master turns up. It is also a full explainer of the same topic, so it competes with our own chalk animation rather than adding to it.
beat: 2-3 (sound path, cochlea) at most as a brief reference; better as a reference for our own animation

title: Data to synthesize an honest otoacoustic emission (no PD/CC0 recording found)
url: https://www.ehdi-pals.org/HostedMaterials/Otoacoustic emissions their origin in cochlear function and use.pdf
creator: Kemp DT, Br Med Bull 2002;63:223-241; plus Abdala, Luo & Shera, JASA 2017 141(3):1874 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5848845); StatPearls 'Otoacoustic Emissions' (https://www.statpearls.com/articlelibrary/viewarticle/142885); Interacoustics TEOAE protocol page (https://www.interacoustics.com/oae-devices/lyra/support/creating-a-teoae-pass-refer-protocol)
license_quote: Facts only are used (facts are not copyrightable). Abdala 2017: "(c) 2017 Acoustical Society of America."
why: Use these for numbers; the sound itself we synthesize and label as a simulation. SOAEs (Kemp 2002): "typically highly stable pure tones of level -10 to 30 dB SPL", "found in 30-40% of healthy young ears". Abdala 2017: about 85% of newborns versus 51-68% of young adults have SOAEs; adult females 65% vs males 36%; mean frequency about 2400 Hz in young adults and 3000-4445 Hz in newborns (newborn range 1000-9800 Hz); mean level about 4 dB SPL in adults and 9-11.3 dB SPL in newborns; above 30 dB SPL is rare. StatPearls gives SOAE frequencies of 500-4500 Hz. TEOAE (Kemp 2002): click "around 84 dB SPL peak equivalent"; healthy infant responses "15 dB SPL to more than 30 dB SPL"; analysis window about 3.5-12 ms after the click; strongest at 1-4 kHz, up to 6-7 kHz in young ears. StatPearls: latency 2-23 ms, high frequencies return first. Interacoustics: screening clicks at 80-84 dB SPL, non-linear click, analysis from 4 ms. DPOAE (StatPearls): f2/f1 = 1.2, L1-L2 = 10 dB, 55-65 dB SPL primaries, response largest at 2f1-f2.

title: Britannica, Ear: Cochlea (structure of the cochlea)
creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
license_quote: Numbers only, quoted as facts.
why: "coiled two and one-half turns around a hollow central pillar"; cone "approximately 9 mm (0.35 inch) in diameter at its base" and "5 mm in height"; tube "approximately 30 mm in length"; "widest - 2 mm" at the basal coil; "In humans the basilar membrane is about 30 to 35 mm in length"; "It widens from less than 0.1 mm near its basal end to 0.5 mm near the apex."

title: Liu et al. 2015, Macromolecular organization and fine structure of the human basilar membrane, Cell Tissue Res 360:245-262
creator: Liu W, Atturo F, Aldaya R, ... Rask-Andersen H
license_quote: Open Access, Creative Commons Attribution License (facts only used; no figures reused).
why: Basilar membrane "34-mm-long"; width "ranged from 126 um at the base to 418 um in the apex" (one specimen; 144.5 um lower basal, 352 um lower apical turn); thickness 0.55-1.16 um; scala tympani width 1.29 mm (lower basal) to 0.57 mm (apex); about 15,000 hair cells in total. Figures are CC-BY, so use the numbers only.

title: van der Jagt et al. 2017, Variations in cochlear duct shape revealed on clinical CT images, Sci Rep 7:17566
creator: van der Jagt AMA, Kalkman RK, Briaire JJ, Verbist BM, Frijns JHM
license_quote: Facts only used.
why: Outer-wall length for the first two turns: median 35.1 mm (range 30.3-41.5 mm, 479 ears). Duct diameter 2.6 mm near the round window, narrowing to 1.5 mm at about 500 degrees. Cites Erixon et al.: basal-turn diameter (A value) 5.6-8.2 mm. Large natural variation, so any value in range is defensible.

title: Cochlea.eu: Hair cells overview and Outer Hair Cells (OHCs)
creator: Pujol R. et al., cochlea.eu (Montpellier)
license_quote: Site: "Copyright 2024 | cochlea.eu | All Rights Reserved"; "This product may not be copied or used for profit." Numbers only.
why: Numbers only (none of the images): about 3,500 inner hair cells and about 12,000 outer hair cells ("ten to twelve thousands") in 3 rows; outer hair cell length "a 25 um basal OHC ... codes for 20 kHz" rising to about 70 um at the apex (below 100 Hz); diameter constant at 7 um; W-shaped staircase bundles of about 100 stereocilia in 3 rows. Second source for counts: BioNumbers 117129 (https://bionumbers.hms.harvard.edu/bionumber.aspx?id=117129), from Ashmore 2008 Physiol Rev, gives about 3,500 inner and 11,000 outer hair cells.

title: Greenwood place-frequency function (human constants), via Buechner et al. 2025, Front Neurosci 19:1624499
creator: Buechner A, Weller T, Penninger RT, ... Schurzig D (citing Greenwood 1990)
license_quote: Facts only used.
why: f = A(10^(a*x) - k) with "A = 165.4, a = 2.1 and k = 0.88", where x is relative length from apex (x=0) to base (x=1); average basilar membrane 35 mm. Computed here: apex about 20 Hz, base about 20.7 kHz. Use it to place frequency labels along the Blender spiral and to drive the travelling-wave peak position.
